articles.title: Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb are being let down by Dallas Cowboys defense again, says Phoebe Schecter
articles.summary: Watch the NFL's Thanksgiving triple-header live on Sky Sports from 5pm Thursday, starting with Chicago Bears at Detroit Lions, followed by the Philadelphia Eagles against the Dallas Cowboys and Patrick Mahomes's Kansas City Chiefs versus Josh Allen's Buffalo Bills from 1.20am Friday
articles.body:
Prescott and the Cowboys are 5-6 and second in the NFC East as they face their divisional rival Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving Thursday, live on Sky Sports NFL.

Dallas leaned on their offense once again in Week 11 when they stormed to a 51-30 win over the Tennessee Titans behind four touchdown passes from Prescott and 100-yard receiving games for both CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.

It is an offense ranked second in passing and third in scoring, but hindered by a defense that has slumped to second-worst in yards, fifth-worst against the pass, dead last in rushing and fourth-worst in scoring. Deja vu in Dallas.

"It never has been Dak's fault," said Sky Sports NFL's Phoebe Schecter. "For years now, Dak Prescott has done a phenomenal job.

"Originally it was only him and CeeDee Lamb. You bring in George Pickens last year, they've upped the game. He is now able to spread that ball out, both of them contested catchers, yards after the catch.

"They're so much fun to watch, but there's always one side that's letting them down. And it's so hard to not look at this defense."

Prescott is currently 276 of 420 [65.7 per cent] passing for 3,049 yards - second only to Joe Burrow in the league - and 25 touchdowns to six interceptions. Lamb, meanwhile, is ranked second behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba with 1,108 receiving yards, followed by Pickens down in 11th with 780 as part of one of football's most dominant aerial trios.

But it will mean nothing if the Cowboys continue to be haunted by long-term issues on defense.

"And even with everything that's gone on with defensive coordinator Christian Parker and Mike Pettine, and you get Caleb Downs, who's supposed to be one of the best [young defenders] out there," Schecter added.

"You must be so frustrated if you're Dak Prescott in this offense. And Brian Schottenheimer is doing all he can to keep that positivity.

"But man, when you've got a quarterback that can do that and then a defense that can't stop anything, it is so frustrating."

The Cowboys switched play-calling duties from under-fire defensive coordinator Christian Parker to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine for the first time against the Titans in Week 11. Still, they shipped 30 points against one of the NFL's struggling teams.

They now take on an Eagles team coming off a 19-16 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers to end a seven-game losing streak.

Dallas are trailing the New York Giants (6-3-1) at the top of the division, and face fresh competition from the Washington Commanders after they moved to 4-5-1 with a shock win over the Cincinnati Bengals.

articles.title: Bills' Josh Allen Teams with Oscar-Winning Director for New Documentary Premiering on HBO
articles.summary: A chance encounter between Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen and two-time Oscar-winning director Ben Proudfoot led to the pair working together on a new documentary that premieres Tuesday on HBO.
articles.body:
A chance encounter between Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen and two-time Oscar-winning director Ben Proudfoot led to the pair working together on a new documentary that premieres Tuesday on HBO.

As reported by John Wawrow of the Associated Press, Proudfoot initially didn't know who Allen was when he saw a cutout of the NFL star standing in a McDonald's restaurant while working in Buffalo.

Around the same time, Allen's Out of Pocket production company was just being launched. He was shown Proudfoot's latest work, which aims to capture the heroism and community spirit of the region during the two-day blizzard that led to 28 deaths in winter 2022 , before the pair agreed to work together on it as the company's first output.

Exec: Josh Allen 'Scariest Player Ever' 😱

"Who knows the reason that I started Out of Pocket," Allen said, per Wawrow. "Maybe it was for this exact moment to push this film forward and for the world to see because of what I think Buffalo and western New York stand for, the grittiness, the care for one another. We're called the 'City of Good Neighbors,' and this totally encapsulates that."

"I think it speaks volumes that the story [Allen] chose to inaugurate his company with is about the goodness of the people of Buffalo," Proudfoot noted, per Wawrow. "He could do anything. He decided to make a film about the heroism of everyday folks from Buffalo."

articles.title: Jerry Jones Addresses Criticism of Christian Parker Hire and Cowboys DC's Future After Major Change
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones isn't ready to say his team made a mistake by hiring Christian Parker as a first-time defensive coordinator this offseason.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones isn't ready to say his team made a mistake by hiring Christian Parker as a first-time defensive coordinator this offseason.

Parker, the youngest DC in Cowboys history , was demoted as defensive playcaller in favor of Mike Pettine ahead of last Sunday's 51-30 win over the Tennessee Titans.

Jones said after the victory he was "hesitant to use the word miss" regarding the choice of Parker as DC, per ESPN's Todd Archer .

Clark Addresses Pettine-Parker Relationship

"We didn't miss the fact that he'd never called plays while he was young, and we didn't miss the fact that that can be a disadvantage as opposed to someone that's done it a lot, call plays," Jones said, per Archer.

"But it was made up for (with) his unique people skills, his unique impact that he can have with players, young players. So he has so many qualities, and boy, he's going to be in coaching. He'll be in coaching for a long time to come."

Jones also indicated he felt there was a possibility Parker's next shot at coaching could come in Dallas, despite The Athletic's Jonathan Jones recently reporting that "multiple sources expect Parker to coach for another team in 2027."

"He hadn't been in the foxhole and hit with the full burden of coordinator and calling plays. He hadn't had that happen," Jones said. "Well, you can't have it happen, if you're young enough. This was a hard hit on the nose. Very visible. Everybody recognized that. That shouldn't take away at all with how outstanding he is."

Jones concluded, "I would say it's more a fact that he'll be calling plays again in the NFL, and maybe with the Dallas Cowboys."

Parker last called defensive plays in Week 10, when the Cowboys allowed a home franchise-record 584 yards against by the 49ers.

With Pettine on the mic for the first time since 2020 the following week, the Cowboys allowed 346 yards from a 1-9 Titans team that has consistently struggled to generate offense this season.

"That would be inaccurate to say the change was the reason that we won today, or the reason that we played a certain way on the defensive side of the ball. That's too much," Jones told reporters . "But I did like the things that we were doing.

"We did some of what we did today last week against San Francisco, defensively. We played a little sounder today, but it wasn't San Francisco that we were out there playing today, either, and we all recognize that. But this is a far better game than it could have been under these circumstances."

The Cowboys have a short turnaround before Pettine gets his second shot at calling plays this season during a Thanksgiving matchup against the visiting Philadelphia Eagles.

Whether the Dallas defense is able to take another step forward could impact both the NFC East playoff race and whether Jones and head coach Brian Schottenheimer keep Pettine in his new role down the stretch of the season.

articles.title: Robert Saleh's Titans Hot Seat Updated by NFL Insider After Viral Comments on Loss to Cowboys
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh caused a stir with his viral comments after Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Dallas Cowboys, but it sounds like his job remains safe for now.
articles.body:
Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh caused a stir with his viral comments after Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Dallas Cowboys, but it sounds like his job remains safe for now.

On Tuesday's episode of The Breer Report , Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer received a question from a fan about whether Saleh could be one-and-done with the Titans, and he responded, "I would say probably not."

Saleh had called out his team after Sunday's loss for playing "disgusting, embarrassing football," and he added, "That starts with me. I got to figure it out."

The Titans fell to 1-9 following their loss to the Cowboys, which marked their third straight game giving up at least 40 points. Despite being known for his defensive acumen, Saleh leads a Tennessee team that ranks last in the NFL with 399.8 total yards allowed per game.

Still, Breer noted that there are "a number of things" that have to be taken into account while assessing Saleh's job security. The Titans traded their two best defensive players, safety Amani Hooker and defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, at this month's deadline for extra draft capital.

"They're now loaded with draft picks over the next couple of years, and they really should have a chance to restock there... The bottom line is, they're gonna have a chance to rework the roster around the coaching staff that we have on hand right now when we get to April," Breer explained.

Saleh also appears to have brought some stability to the Titans amid their disappointing season, as Breer went on to indicate that he may have already won over the organization.

"I do think through a lot of bumps over the course of the last three, four, five months, Robert Saleh has been a steady hand," Breer said. "I think that's what the organization needs right now... I think Saleh has maintained a good atmosphere in that building. I think he's been the right man to guide them through what was always gonna be, I think, a tough year from a wins-and-losses standpoint."

Breer added that the development of the Titans' top young players like second-year quarterback Cam Ward and rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate over the final seven games of the season will help determine Saleh's future in Tennessee.

The Titans will try to show some signs of a bright future when they face the Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3) on Sunday.

articles.title: Eli Manning, Rob Gronkowski Among 52 Players to Make Cut in Pro Football HOF Class of 2027 Voting
articles.summary: The Pro Football Hall of Fame narrowed the list of prospective candidates for induction to 52.
articles.body:
The Pro Football Hall of Fame narrowed the list of prospective candidates for induction to 52.

The Hall said that 50 players typically move on, but anybody who's tied for 50th qualifies. Eli Manning, Adrian Peterson, Rob Gronkowski, Richard Sherman, Earl Thomas III, LC. Greenwood, Vince Wilfork, James Harrison and Terrell Suggs are some of the notable legends who have a chance of earning a bust in Canton, Ohio, in 2027:

The list will be halved to 25 during the next phase of voting, and 13 will eventually reach the finalist stage.

At least two players look sure bets to go into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility.

Thanks to injuries, Gronkowski doesn't have the same longevity as other elite tight ends. At his peak, he was the most dominant player ever at the position. From 2011-15, he averaged 78.3 receiving yards per game and had 55 touchdown grabs in 64 appearances.

Peterson ranks fifth all time in yards (14,918) and touchdowns (120) on the ground. He remains the last non-quarterback to win MVP, which he earned by running for 2,097 yards in 2012.

The HOF voting committee is entitled to pick between three and seven candidates for induction. Assuming former New England Patriots coach Bill Belichick isn't snubbed again, there might effectively be just four spots up for grabs if Gronkowski and Peterson are first-timers.

Some worthy figures are bound to miss out because of that.

Greenwood, Torry Holt and Reggie Wayne are all seven-time finalists . Willie Anderson has gotten there five times. Their waits could continue given the depth of talent that joined the ballot.

articles.title: NFL Playoff Picture entering Week 12: Thanksgiving games could shake up postseason seeding
articles.summary: Thursday's showdown against the Chiefs holds significant playoff implications, even if the AFC East is all but wrapped up.
articles.body:
The AFC field is by no means set. But it's a lot more firmed up than what's happening on the NFC side of things.

The 49ers might be steamrolling toward the top seed in the conference, coming off a rousing victory over the Vikings, but the rest of the seeding remains up for grabs. All four NFC North teams remain in our projected playoff field as of now, but two West teams (Rams and Seahawks) are still very much in the mix.

Losses by the Jaguars and Ravens have added a little more drama, and the seeding order remains in flux. The results of Thursday's Chiefs-Bills game could also upset the order even more.

Here's how the seeding would line up if the playoffs started today.

The weird thing about the Bills lately is that they're winning more with defense and less with Josh Allen. Buffalo hasn't allowed a touchdown in 11 straight quarters. Since the bye, the Bills have allowed 37 points in four games — granted, against more challenged offenses, but it's still an improvement. Allen's recent struggles can't be glossed over; he hasn't been the same passer the past few weeks, and he didn't scramble once Sunday. Thursday's showdown against the Chiefs holds significant playoff implications, even if the AFC East is all but wrapped up.

Denver's offense found some footing with a big game from Jonah Coleman, and even with some missed opportunities, the passing game did well enough against the Raiders. The Broncos' defense isn't the lockdown unit it has been in recent seasons, but still comes up with timely plays and a hearty pass rush. By virtue of tiebreakers, the Broncos hold the slimmest of margins over the Chiefs for first place, but you can bet this one will go right down to the wire after the teams split their meetings this season. Denver's schedule lines up incredibly well, even with three of the next four games on the road and a Christmas home game against the Bills. Only the Buccaneers have a lower opponents win percentage for their remaining games.

Their disappointing loss to the Giants notwithstanding, the Jaguars still profile as a dangerous team. They scored one touchdown in six red-zone trips against the Giants, with one dubious call robbing them of a TD . It was a fluky outing, and the Jaguars still could easily have won. The Jags' defense looks strong, and Jacksonville still owns the league's best point differential at plus-125. Trevor Lawrence faced some real pressure against the Giants, and it's a blueprint other teams will try to copy. The Jags still have a few tough road tests ahead of them, but the path is there for 11-plus wins, a division title and a chance to move up in seeding.

Monday night was a major disappointment . Maybe the weather had something to do with the early-game struggles, but the Commanders' defense seemed to frustrate what had been a red-hot Bengals offense. Then the defense allowed six straight scoring drives, and the Bengals now have only a one-game lead in the AFC North. The Bengals have been better overall on defense this season, but poor efforts against the likes of the Titans and Commanders open the door for questioning just how good they are. They're still near-locks to make the postseason the way things are going, but the Bengals can't keep counting on Joe Burrow being lights-out every single time out.

The Chiefs have managed two games without Kenneth Walker III, scoring a combined 69 points and hitting triple digits in rush yards both outings, with rookie Emmett Johnson up to the challenge. Patrick Mahomes has been on a tear the past four games, and the Chiefs have allowed the fewest points in the league this season. The parts are there to make another Super Bowl run after the lost season in 2025. Some usual suspects stand in the way — the Broncos in the division, and the Bills, whom they visit on Thanksgiving.

They've been living dangerously, with all six of their victories by four points or fewer. But heading into the bye last week with the comeback win over the Texans was a great confidence booster, especially with the Steelers scuttling. The Browns' offense still has work to do, but that unit has shown signs of improvement in recent games. The defense has been opportunistic, keeping the team in games until the offense can find a spark. There's a real path to a wild-card spot, and the division is not out of reach, with two games left against the Bengals, including two weeks from now in Cleveland.

Things are looking a bit dire in Pittsburgh, with Aaron Rodgers struggling and DK Metcalf hurting his team . Their offense can't find a real groove, and the defense is competitive, but the pass rush has been inconsistent. The AFC North door is not slammed shut yet, and the Steelers will be in the mix, but the schedule offers a few tough games, and the team feels like it's in a rut after two straight losses. Did the bye week hurt the Steelers? They'd won four straight before that.

What a statement the 49ers delivered in Mexico City, leaning on a Vikings defense that was receiving "generational" labels coming in. This offense has looked like it could score on almost any drive since the bye. Whatever happened in the Falcons loss, it's been flushed right out of the 49ers' systems. Another promising development against the Vikings was the play of the defense, which was coming off its worst outing of the season in Dallas. If the Niners can show the kind of balance they did in Week 11, they're the clear favorites for the conference's top seed and the bye, but injuries ( Colton McKivitz the latest ) continue to haunt them.

The Lions started playing inspired defense before Aidan Hutchinson got hurt, and they've continued their strong play since he landed on injured reserve. The returns of Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph have been huge, too, and they could be the backbone of this unit down the stretch. Thursday's game against the Bears might be one of the biggest in the teams' history, which goes back to the 1930s (depending on whether you follow it back to the Portsmouth Spartans days). Two dangerous offenses, ready to take flight. What a game to start Thanksgiving.

There were plenty of holes to poke in the Giants' overall résumé, but Sunday's victory over the Jaguars was a narrative changer (even if it came with a very favorable call going their way ). The defense, especially Abdul Carter, played determined football, rushed the passer and forced turnovers. That formula can work if J.J. McCarthy keeps taking care of the ball and making positive plays. Head coach John Harbaugh has been pretty conservative, and there have been some late-game hiccups, but the Jaguars game showed some real grit. The NFC East is theirs for the taking, even with Washington and Dallas within reach.

Two straight wins, but hoo boy, neither one was easy. Sunday was only their second home win of the season, and they have four more left in Charlotte, but not before two big ones on the road: at Tampa Bay and at Minnesota. Carolina is back to .500, and with the Bucs and Saints losing Sunday, it's a two-game lead in the NFC South. A win over the Bucs next week would put the Panthers in a dominant position for the division. Do we trust them? Last season became a game of pat-a-cake back and forth until it was decided by tiebreaker. Bryce Young and the defense have been a little too up and down this season.

Sunday's win over the Saints was one of the Bears' uglier games of the season and another sign that their offense can be prone to some sleepier outings, but Chicago showed it can win games with its defense, too. The remaining schedule is an absolute meat grinder, starting with Thursday's epic in Detroit, where the Bears have not won since 2021. This looks like a dangerous Bears team in any setting, and they're going to face some of the best of the best over the next month-plus. How they handle this gauntlet of a schedule could tell us a lot about whether the Bears can make a Super Bowl run.

The loss to the 49ers was a major blow, taking it on the chin against the NFC's elite and dropping the Vikings below the Bears. The Vikings still have an incredible defense, but it was humbled by Brock Purdy and the 49ers. Kirk Cousins was excellent against the Packers but less so against the 49ers. It wasn't enough to sour things completely, but the Vikings know they have to play better than they did in Mexico City to compete in a deep, talented NFC field. There's still a chance to steal the NFC North, and the next string of games (Falcons, Panthers and Patriots) gives them a chance to regain their footing.

The return of Micah Parsons , plus Josh Jacobs eventually, could give this team a boost coming out of the bye. The Packers will need it heading into a stretch of games that includes the Rams, Bills, Bears and Lions. Green Bay has been so up and down this season that it's hard to get a gauge for what this team could be — and will be — come playoff time. There's no guarantee the Packers will get in the postseason, with a tough schedule and the Rams, Seahawks and others still breathing down their necks. Can Jordan Love deliver another hot stretch of ball upcoming? They're going to need it.

articles.title: Greg Newsome Injury Update, Latest NFL Rumors on Return Timeline from Surgery for Giants CB
articles.summary: The New York Giants will reportedly be without one of their top cornerbacks for at least the next month.
articles.body:
The New York Giants will reportedly be without one of their top cornerbacks for at least the next month.

Greg Newsome II is set to undergo tightrope surgery on his high ankle sprain and will be sidelined for "roughly" four to six weeks, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported Tuesday.

Giants coach John Harbaugh said Monday Newsome had suffered a "serious" high ankle sprain during Sunday's win over the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Harbaugh said at the time Newsome would likely miss "multiple weeks" but that he was unsure as of Monday whether the injury necessitated surgery.

Newsome, who inked a three-year, $46 million extension with the Giants earlier this month, suffered his injury on the opening drive after taking four snaps in Sunday's 23-18 win over the Jaguars.

The Athletic's Dan Duggan reported the Giants "taped [Newsome] up and he tried to run on the sideline but was clearly hobbled" before he was ruled out of the game. He was spotted wearing a walking boot in the locker room after the win, per the New York Post 's Ryan Dunleavy .

Paulson Adebo, who was a healthy scratch at the back of a cornerback depth chart led by Newsome and Deonte Banks the week prior, stepped up Sunday after Newsome exited against the Jaguars.

Adebo allowed just two catches for 49 yards on eight targets while breaking up two passes and recording an interception, per Pro Football Focus' Bradley Locker .

Harbaugh said after the game Adebo had received a game ball after playing Sunday "like the top-level corner that he is."

Banks also recorded three pass breakups and recorded an interception of his own in the win over the Jaguars.

Harbaugh will hope to get another strong performance from the team's current top corner duo of Banks and Adebo as the Giants (6-3-1) look to maintain their NFC East lead over the Dallas Cowboys (5-6) when kicking off a Sunday matchup at the Indianapolis Colts.

articles.title: Kenneth Walker III Injury Update, Latest News on Status for Chiefs vs. Bills on Thanksgiving
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III, who has missed the last two games with a groin injury, returned to practice on Tuesday as his team gets ready for a Thanksgiving night matchup at the Buffalo Bills.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III, who has missed the last two games with a groin injury , returned to practice on Tuesday as his team gets ready for a Thanksgiving night matchup at the Buffalo Bills.

Head coach Andy Reid told reporters on Tuesday that Walker wasn't expected to do "a ton of work."

Walker was ultimately listed as a limited participant in practice.

Walker has been exceptional for the 8-2 Chiefs, totaling 1,044 yards from scrimmage and 11 touchdowns in eight games.

The reigning Super Bowl MVP arrived in town after the Chiefs signed the ex-Seattle Seahawk to a three-year, $43.1 million contract . He's been a driving force for the Chiefs' turnaround after Kansas City went 6-11 last season.

Unfortunately, Walker suffered the injury during his team's Thursday, Nov. 12 practice. Reid characterized the injury as a "sore groin."

"It's getting better," Reid told reporters last Wednesday. We just don't want to do something stupid. He's feeling better."

Rookie Emmett Johnson has taken his place over the last two weeks, which has featured the Chiefs outscoring the Atlanta Falcons (35-13) and Arizona Cardinals (34-7) by 49 points. During that stretch, Johnson has rushed for 206 yards and a touchdown while adding 108 receiving yards and two scores on 10 receptions.

Ultimately, the Chiefs got the best of both worlds. They enjoyed a pair of comfortable wins while Walker was able to rest and get right for the stretch run.

Walker missed the team's walkthrough on Monday, but his Tuesday practice participation, even in a limited capacity, is a good sign for his availability on Thursday.

It's a massive game for the Chiefs, who are (a) tied with the 8-2 Denver Broncos for the AFC West lead and (b) simultaneously trying to chase down the 9-1 Bills for the AFC's No. 1 spot.

We'll see if Walker is out there soon enough. Kickoff in Buffalo is set for 8:20 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Stefon Diggs caught shouting ‘Throw the f***ing ball’ as Jayden Daniels and Commanders struggle against Bengals
articles.summary: Stefon Diggs could not hide his frustration as the Washington Commanders struggled to get their offense going against the Cincinnati Bengals on Monday
articles.body: Stefon Diggs could not hide his frustration as the Washington Commanders struggled to get their offense going against the Cincinnati Bengals on Monday night. The wide receiver was caught shouting on the sideline during the second quarter after Washington failed to make much progress on its opening drives. His words appeared to be directed at someone on the Commanders' sideline, although the television footage did not make it clear who he was addressing. However, the outburst came before Jayden Daniels helped Washington turn things around and secure a dramatic 22-20 victory.Stefon Diggs Shows His Frustration as Jayden Daniels and Commanders Offense Struggle Against BengalsThe Commanders had a difficult start at Northwest Stadium on November 23. Their first four offensive possessions ended with punts, and they managed to cover only 27 yards during those drives. Meanwhile, the Bengals had built a 10-0 lead, leaving Washington struggling to find an answer.Stefon Diggs was also having a quiet start. The 32-year-old receiver had received just one target and had not made a catch when cameras caught his angry reaction on the sideline."Hey! Throw the f***ing ball!" Diggs appeared to shout during the broadcast.A member of the Commanders' staff then tried to move him away from the area, but the receiver continued expressing his frustration near the bench.It was not clear whether Diggs was speaking directly to quarterback Jayden Daniels or someone else on the team. However, his reaction came at a time when Washington's passing game was struggling to get going.According to The Washington Post, neither the person Diggs was addressing nor the exact reason for his outburst was clear from the video. The broadcast did show his frustration as the Commanders searched for a way back into the game.The receiver eventually got his first catch late in the second quarter. Daniels found him for a 10-yard gain, helping Washington move into Bengals territory.That play also gave the home side some much-needed momentum after a difficult opening stretch.Jayden Daniels Leads Washington Commanders to 22-20 Win After Stefon Diggs' Sideline OutburstWashington made the most of its late first-half possession. Running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt finished the drive with a one-yard touchdown run after the Commanders moved down the field on a nine-play possession.The score brought Washington within three points, and the teams went into halftime with Cincinnati leading 10-7.The Commanders were much better after the break. Daniels helped the offense find its rhythm, and Washington put together six straight scoring drives without punting again.Diggs also became more involved as the game went on. He finished with four catches for 45 yards on six targets, according to the game statistics.However, the Bengals continued to make things difficult. Joe Burrow threw for 300 yards and two touchdowns, while Cincinnati managed to take a 20-19 lead with only 46 seconds left.Washington still had one chance to win the game.With 39 seconds remaining and no timeouts, Daniels connected with rookie receiver Antonio Williams for a 22-yard gain. He then found Williams again for a 42-yard pass that took the Commanders to the Cincinnati eight-yard line.Daniels got the team into position to attempt a field goal, and rookie kicker Drew Stevens made no mistake. His 26-yard kick went through as time expired, giving Washington a 22-20 win.The victory also ended Cincinnati's five-game winning streak.Diggs' sideline reaction became one of the notable moments from the game, but Washington's comeback was built on a much stronger second half. Daniels finished with 289 passing yards and 55 rushing yards, while Williams recorded nine catches for 122 yards.The late comeback was especially important for Washington, which had looked completely out of rhythm during the opening quarter. Daniels finished the night with 23 completions on 35 attempts and did not throw an interception. Stevens also converted all five of his field-goal attempts.The win gave the Commanders back-to-back victories and stopped the Bengals from extending their winning run to six games.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Micah Parsons Injury Update, Latest on Star's Return Timeline Ahead of Packers vs. Rams
articles.summary: Micah Parsons is back.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers star edge rusher, sidelined since Dec. 14 of last year with a torn ACL and meniscus, has been cleared to play and is set to make his season debut against the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday, the team confirmed on Tuesday.

Michael Irvin Talks Cowboys, Super Bowl, Packers vs. Rams and Miami QB Mensah in B/R Interview

Speaking to reporters on Monday, Parsons said he still needed final clearance before being activated.

"I really don't know yet," he said Monday. "I still gotta talk to (Dr. Neal) ElAttrache, I still gotta get cleared from my surgical doctor, so we'll see."

He said he had to have a conference call with his doctor, in which they'd go over testing and other metrics to make sure he's "100 percent ready."

"I feel like I've done everything I possibly could to put myself in position to potentially play on Wednesday but for sure this season," Parsons said.

Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said last week that the team planned for Parsons to be available for Wednesday's game against the Rams, though he clarified that Parsons still had a "couple more hurdles to clear."

Parsons cleared those hurdles and is now set to return to action for the first time in nearly a year.

In his last fully healthy season in 2023, Parsons was tremendous, recording 64 tackles and 14 sacks as a member of the Dallas Cowboys. While he missed the last three games of the season last year, he still recorded 41 tackles and 12.5 sacks.

He has some rust to shake off, but will look to return to that form this year.

Parsons' return comes amid a 6-4 start to the year for the Packers, who are hoping to finish the year strong and make a deep playoff run. Green Bay currently sits in last place in the loaded NFC North but is still in playoff position.

But a win over the Rams this week could go a long way, as Los Angeles is also 6-4 and looking to move ahead of the Packers in the standings.

Picking up a win against the Rams gets much easier with Parsons now back in the fold.

Ahead of the holidays, Caleb Williams is already giving thanks.

The quarterback also told quite the story in one of the huddles:

articles.title: Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs Hyped as OPOY Contender by Bears' Ben Johnson Ahead of Thanksgiving Clash
articles.summary: Before the Detroit Lions face the Chicago Bears in a Thanksgiving NFC North showdown, Bears coach Ben Johnson had plenty of kind words for one of his opponents.
articles.body:
Before the Detroit Lions face the Chicago Bears in a Thanksgiving NFC North showdown, Bears coach Ben Johnson had plenty of kind words for one of his opponents.

Johnson, who used to be the offensive coordinator for the Lions, said he believed Detroit running back Jahmyr Gibbs should be an Offensive Player of the Year candidate this year.

"If he's not the offensive player of the year right now, then he has to be top three …," Johnson said on Tuesday, per ESPN's Courtney Cronin . "Seems like they can't get him the ball enough."

Gibbs is averaging 4.9 yards per carry for the Lions this season and has rushed for 13 touchdowns, the most in the league. His 1,098 total yards are the most rushing yards in the NFL this season. His 109.8 yards per game also top the leaderboards.

The Bears and Lions are tied at 8-2 atop the NFC North standings heading into their first matchup of the season. Chicago is coming off a win against the New Orleans Saints this Sunday while the Lions beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

The Bears allow 4.5 yards per carry, the eighth-most in the NFL, making the matchup against Gibbs all the more important.

articles.title: Ben Roethlisberger, Eli Manning, Antonio Brown among players advancing in Pro Football Hall of Fame voting process for 2027 class
articles.summary: On Tuesday, the Hall announced 52 players who have moved forward in their candidacy for next year's class.
articles.body:
A pair of quarterbacks from the fabled 2004 draft class, Pittsburgh Steelers legend Ben Roethlisberger and New York Giants icon Eli Manning, plus embattled wide receiver Antonio Brown, are among the 52 players the Pro Football Hall of Fame revealed are advancing in the voting process for the 2027 class.

Per current Hall of Fame bylaws, at this stage of that process, selectors cast ballots for 50 players they believe should move forward in their candidacy, but those tied for the 50th position also remain eligible for induction.

The list the Hall announced on Tuesday will next be cut down to 25 players. That more exclusive group will be unveiled in about two weeks.

For now, here's a position-by-position breakdown of the players being considered for enshrinement:

Ben Roethlisberger, Eli Manning, Ken Anderson

Shaun Alexander, Frank Gore, Marshawn Lynch, LeSean McCoy, Adrian Peterson, Fred Taylor, Ricky Watters

Anquan Boldin, Antonio Brown, Rob Gronkowski, Torry Holt, Billy "White Shoes" Johnson, Steve Smith Sr., Otis Taylor, Hines Ward, Reggie Wayne, Jason Witten

Rodney Harrison, Lester Hayes, Albert Lewis, Eddie Meador, Richard Sherman, Earl Thomas III, Everson Walls, Darren Woodson

John Abraham, Geno Atkins, L.C. Greenwood, Jim Marshall, Robert Mathis, Haloti Ngata, Vince Wilfork, Kevin Williams

Maxie Baughan, London Fletcher, James Harrison, Karl Mecklenburg, Tommy Nobis, Terrell Suggs

Roethlisberger and Manning draw the eye, considering they each quarterbacked historic franchises to a pair of Super Bowl victories; however, this cohort is understandably littered with household names.

Running back Adrian Peterson is forever part of Minnesota Vikings lore. He's one of the nine NFL players to ever rush for 2,000 yards in a season. In fact, Peterson's 2,097 yards on the ground in 2012 were the second most in a single-season in league history , behind only the 2,105 rushing yards Eric Dickerson logged while starring for the Los Angeles Rams in 1984. Peterson earned NFL MVP honors that season.

Another RB in the running, Frank Gore, is the NFL's third all-time leading rusher . Gore spent the bulk of his career with the San Francisco 49ers. Even in his 16th and final campaign, he was still somewhat productive, amassing 653 rushing yards in his age-37 season with the New York Jets in 2020.

Rob Gronkowski and Jason Witten are both integral to the annals of tight end play. Gronkowski was a red-zone monster, finishing his 11-season career with a whopping 92 receiving touchdowns. Together, he and seven-time Super Bowl-winning quarterback Tom Brady authored one of the most electrifying duos in the sport, first with the New England Patriots and then with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. As for Witten, he proved to be one of the NFL's most reliable security blankets to date, maxing out with 110 catches during his 2012 campaign with the Dallas Cowboys.

Interestingly, beleaguered wideout Antonio Brown was among the players included in 52-man list the Hall put forth on Tuesday. Brown was a superstar during the peak of his head-scratching 12-season run in the league. He built most of his résumé in Pittsburgh, where he stacked seven 1,000-yard receiving seasons. In his nine-season stay with the Steelers, he led the NFL in receiving yards twice: first in 2014 and again in 2017. He also led the league in touchdown catches in 2018.

But the end of Brown's career was marred by the trouble he got himself into, on and off the field. Earlier this month, in a Miami court, Brown pleaded guilty to aggravated assault following a 2025 shooting incident.

Brown still has long odds of being inducted next year. Ultimately, 13 players will make up most of the 15 finalists who will be presented at the selection committee's annual meeting. The other two candidates will be Bill Belichick (who emerged from the "coach" category) and Patriots owner Robert Kraft (who came out of the "contributor" category) .

The Hall's 2027 class will be announced at "NFL Honors" in February.

articles.title: J.K. Dobbins Suspended by Broncos for Black Friday NFL Game vs. Steelers
articles.summary: Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton told reporters on Tuesday that running back J.K. Dobbins is suspended for Friday's matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers due to conduct detrimental to the team.
articles.body:
Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton told reporters on Tuesday that running back J.K. Dobbins is suspended for Friday's matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers due to conduct detrimental to the team.

Dobbins, 27, was the main man in the rushing game last season for the Broncos when healthy, rushing for 772 yards and four scores across 10 games. But he's largely fallen out of favor in Denver of late, with just 18 carries in the past four games for 54 yards and a touchdown. He had one carry and played in just one snap during Sunday's 38-24 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.

After the game, Payton indicated that Dobbins would still have a role.

"J.K.'s going to be super important for what we're doing in this stretch," he told reporters .

But rookie Jonah Coleman has been a revelation, rushing for 302 yards and six touchdowns in just five games while adding 17 catches for 146 yards. It appears to very much be his backfield now.

With RJ Harvey on injured reserve and Dobbins now suspended, Tyler Badie is the logical option to serve as Coleman's backup on Sunday.

The Broncos are 8-2 and currently sit atop the AFC West, though the Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) are nipping at their heels. As they gun for a division title and potentially the top seed in the AFC, they'll likely do so with Coleman handling the majority of the carries, not Dobbins.

articles.title: Brandon Aiyuk Clears Waivers After 49ers Release, New NFL Rumors on WR's Potential Landing Spots
articles.summary: Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk became an unrestricted free agent after clearing waivers on Tuesday, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk became an unrestricted free agent after clearing waivers on Tuesday, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .

Per Schefter, Aiyuk is expected to draw interest from "a few teams," including the Washington Commanders. He's scheduled to visit with the Commanders on Wednesday.

The 28-year-old, who hasn't played in an NFL game since the 2024 season, was released by the San Francisco 49ers on Monday.

Aiyuk previously signed a four-year extension worth $120 million with the 49ers in Aug. 2024, but ended up suffering a torn ACL, MCL and meniscus in Week 7 of the ensuing season.

San Francisco later voided the guaranteed money in Aiyuk's contract after he "failed to attend meetings" and missed other team activities following his knee surgery, per Michael Silver of The Athletic.

49ers general manager John Lynch eventually confirmed that the wideout wouldn't take the field for the team again on Jan. 21.

Aiyuk was removed from the reserve/left squad list and reinstated on Nov. 9 before Monday's release.

The 28-year-old's ties to the Commanders are evident, as NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that a practice squad contract with Washington was viewed as his "most likely option."

Aiyuk was previously teammates with Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels in college at Arizona State and has a house in the Washington area as well.

Teams interested in Aiyuk will hope that a change of scenery can help him look like his former self, as he racked up 2,357 receiving yards and 15 touchdown catches from 2022-23.

articles.title: Ex-49er Brandon Aiyuk will visit with Commanders after clearing waivers
articles.summary: Brandon Aiyuk might have a new home sooner than later.
articles.body:
Brandon Aiyuk might have a new home sooner than later.

The former 49ers receiver is scheduled to visit with the Washington Commanders. That's according to his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, who told ESPN's Adam Schefter that Aiyuk, 28, will meet with the Commanders on Wednesday.

Aiyuk cleared waivers on Tuesday after being released by the 49ers, concluding a protracted and contentious breakup with the franchise. The NFL recently reinstated Aiyuk from the reserve/left squad list , and the 49ers subsequently cut him.

The Commanders have had a need at wide receiver virtually all season. No. 1 receiver and former All-Pro Terry McLaurin is on season-ending injured reserve due to a torn patellar tendon in his left knee.

McLaurin's injury has pushed offseason acquisition Stefon Diggs to the top of the depth chart alongside rookie Antonio Williams. No other Commanders receiver has more than 16 catches this season.

A third-round draft pick, Williams is emerging as a breakout candidate, most notably via his nine-catch, 122-yard performance in Monday's 22-20 upset of the Cincinnati Bengals . Williams made two of those catches for 64 yards in a 46-second drive that set up Drew Stevens' game-winning field goal as time expired.

But even with Williams' emergence, the Commanders are thin at the position and kicking the tires on whether Aiyuk can still be a meaningful contributor following a two-year absence from football. They'll also need to evaluate whether they can trust Aiyuk to fill his potential role following his multiyear standoff with the 49ers.

Aiyuk sustained a torn ACL and MCL in October 2024 , months after signing a four-year, $120 million extension with the 49ers. He failed to report to team facilities in 2025 for his rehabilitation and recovery from those injuries and has not played football since.

The result was a dispute over a $13 million roster bonus that the 49ers wanted back because of Aiyuk's refusal to report. The 49ers ultimately declared that he was not welcome back with the franchise .

Aiyuk has also behaved erratically off the field, including an incident in which he recorded himself speeding past Levi's Stadium at more than 100 mph and posted it on the internet. That ultimately led to a warrant for his arrest .

At his best, Aiyuk was an All-Pro contributor on a winning 49ers team. He tallied 75 receptions for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns in 2023 for a team that went to the Super Bowl. That campaign led to his $120 million contract, of which $27 million in guarantees was eventually voided .

That was three seasons and a serious knee injury ago, in addition to his two years off from football.

The Commanders, meanwhile, are in the hunt to win the NFC East following Monday's last-second win over the Bengals . At 4-5-1, they're two games behind a first-place Giants team against which they own the season tiebreaker.

If Aiyuk signs with Washington and produces at a portion of the pace he did in 2023, he could be a difference-maker on a team quarterbacked by Jayden Daniels. But the Commanders will have considerably more than Aiyuk's on-field upside to consider before signing him.

articles.title: Sean Payton suspends RB J.K. Dobbins for Friday's game vs. Steelers due to 'conduct detrimental to the team'
articles.summary: Payton did not elaborate on what Dobbins did to earn a suspension from the team.
articles.body:
Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton told reporters Tuesday that he is suspending veteran running back J.K. Dobbins for Friday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Payton said it was due to " conduct detrimental to the team , " and the head coach did not elaborate.

Dobbins is in his second season with the Broncos. He began his career with the Baltimore Ravens and spent the 2024 season with the Los Angeles Chargers before joining Denver last year.

He is currently the team's leading rusher with 324 yards and has three touchdowns on 99 carries.

The veteran running back played in 10 games last year, finishing with 772 yards and four touchdowns. Dobbins had a rookie in the backfield with him in RJ Harvey last year, and Denver brought in another this year in Jonah Coleman.

Dobbins has said he is happy to do whatever he can to contribute to the team, but last week Coleman had his breakout game with 111 yards and three touchdowns in Denver's 38-24 win over Las Vegas.

While Coleman had his best game as a rookie, Dobbins had only one touch. With Payton not elaborating, it is unclear whether the conduct detrimental to the team is related to his reduced role in the offense or coincidental.

Coleman has quickly taken over as the lead back, with 302 yards and six touchdowns on 71 carries in six games.

Denver is the second-best team in the AFC , with an 8-2 record. The Broncos, who split with the Kansas City Chiefs this season, currently hold the tiebreaker over their AFC West rivals.

The Broncos will take on the Steelers on the road on Black Friday. With no Dobbins, Coleman is expected to lead the backfield. Harvey and fellow running back Tyler Badie are currently on IR.

Jaret Patterson and/or Cody Schrader will likely join Coleman in the backfield; both are currently on the practice squad and would need to be signed or elevated.

articles.title: 49ers' Kyle Juszczyk praises Brock Purdy, slams 'Shanahan's system' talk around QB: 'Makes all of us better'

None of the MVP talk, none of the Player of the Year talk — any of that sort of stuff — it truly does not seem to faze him. And I truly don’t think he cares what other people think. That’s what we love about Brock. All he cares about is playing to his potential, and we know how high that can be." Juszczyk, or "Juice" as he’s known by many in the football world, is one of the many veteran leaders in the 49ers locker room, and he’s watched Purdy since day one develop into one himself through hard work and leading by example on the gridiron. Purdy, famously known as one of the most successful "Mr. Irrelevant" selections as the last pick in the 2022 NFL Draft, is in his fifth season and has already helped the 49ers reach a Super Bowl. Yet, there’s still a portion of football fans who believe Purdy is only successful because of various reasons, whether it’s the stars around him, or playing in head coach Kyle Shanahan’s scheme. articles.title: Michael Strahan’s daughter Isabella turns her difficult cancer battle into a powerful mission to support children fighting the disease
articles.summary: For Isabella Strahan, returning to normal life after cancer meant more than getting back to college or rebuilding her strength.
articles.body: For Isabella Strahan, returning to normal life after cancer meant more than getting back to college or rebuilding her strength. It also gave her a new perspective on the struggles faced by young patients. Now 22 and cancer-free, Michael Strahan’s daughter is using her experience with a brain tumour to bring comfort to children facing similar challenges. Her latest partnership with Hyundai Hope On Wheels marks an important step in that journey, turning a difficult chapter of her life into an opportunity to make a difference.Isabella Strahan joins Hyundai Hope On Wheels to support children with cancerIsabella recently visited Children’s Hospital of Orange County as part of her partnership with Hyundai USA and Hyundai Hope On Wheels. Rather than simply raising awareness through social media, she spent time with young patients and helped make their hospital experience a little brighter.The visit included handing out special warrior gowns designed to reflect each child's personality. Isabella also joined the children for tea parties and other activities, creating moments of fun in an environment often filled with medical appointments and difficult conversations.“There are so many different gowns for so many different kids and their personalities, so it’s fun to see which one they are gonna choose,” Isabella shared.The initiative focuses on supporting childhood cancer awareness and funding research for better treatments. For Isabella, however, the campaign carries a deeply personal meaning.Having spent months in hospitals herself, she understands how much small gestures and human connections can matter during treatment. Her involvement gives the initiative a powerful personal voice, particularly for children who may feel isolated while dealing with cancer.Michael Strahan’s daughter finds purpose after medulloblastoma battleIsabella's journey began in 2023, when she developed troubling symptoms during her freshman year at the University of Southern California. Persistent headaches, vomiting and balance problems eventually led doctors to discover medulloblastoma, an aggressive brain tumour.Her treatment required emergency brain surgery, radiation and four rounds of chemotherapy. In July 2024, she shared the encouraging news that she was cancer-free.The experience also changed her family. Michael Strahan, who had long supported St. Jude Children's Research Hospital through its campaigns, suddenly faced the reality of his own daughter's cancer diagnosis.“No parent should have to hear that their child has cancer,” he had said in the commercials.Reflecting on the difficult period, Michael explained how the hospital's support became especially meaningful.“[That] line that I used to deliver, usually at the end of the commercial…here I am actually filling that line in my life in real time,”“When I needed that family…they were there for me. I’m just appreciative, and I think things come back to you; give out good, good comes back.”Today, Isabella is rebuilding her life at USC while focusing on fitness, cooking and advocacy. articles.body:
Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn didn't mind the visible frustration shown by wide receiver Stefon Diggs on the sidelines during the team's 22-20 win over the Cincinnati Bengals on Monday night.

"I love his fire, I do," Quinn said after the game, per ESPN's John Keim . "I love that. There's a lot of good that comes with it where it can sound like he's mad but it's like some energy that comes behind it."

"I love the competitor he is," he added. "If something didn't feel right I would step in and address it, but that's not been the case with me."

Diggs was spotted yelling on the sidelines after the Commanders were forced to punt in the second quarter of the game.

At the time, he hadn't recorded a catch as Washington trailed 3-0.

Both Diggs and the Commanders fared much better throughout the remainder of the contest, coming back from a 10-point deficit to emerge victorious over a Bengals squad that entered the game with a 7-2 record.

Diggs finished with four receptions for 45 yards.

The four-time Pro Bowl is in the midst of his first season with Washington after helping the New England Patriots make a Super Bowl appearance during his 2025 campaign.

Through nine games in 2026, Diggs has reeled in 40 catches for 431 yards and six touchdowns.

articles.title: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels Honors Kyren Lacy After Bengals Win
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders picked up their biggest win of the season Monday night, defeating the Cincinnati Bengals in a game they needed to keep their playof...
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders picked up their biggest win of the season Monday night, defeating the Cincinnati Bengals in a game they needed to keep their playoff hopes alive.

Quarterback Jayden Daniels for the second straight week came through when it mattered most, something he's done multiple times throughout his young three-year career.

Daniels completed 23-of-35 passes for 289 yards and added 55 yards on six carries.

But his biggest contribution came with 46 seconds remaining and no timeouts. Trailing 20-19, Daniels completed back-to-back passes to rookie wide receiver Antonio Williams, moving Washington into field goal range despite tight coverage.

Kicker Drew Stevens then drilled a 26-yard field goal as time expired to give the Commanders a 22-20 victory.

Daniels Honors Kyren Lacy in Instagram Post

Following Monday's win, Daniels shared an Instagram post featuring several photos from the game alongside pictures of his former LSU teammate, Kyren Lacy, who died by suicide in April 2025.

"long live k2!" Daniels wrote in the caption.

Among the photos, Daniels included one of Lacy wearing a Commanders jersey and another showing his gravestone.

Lacy once looked poised to follow Daniels into the NFL. While Daniels entered the league in 2024, Lacy prepared for the 2025 NFL Draft. However, legal issues delayed his path to the NFL, and he died two days before a scheduled court appearance that was just two weeks ahead of the draft.

Both players transferred to LSU in 2022 and spent two seasons together. Lacy played a key role in Daniels' Heisman Trophy-winning season in 2023.

He became one of Daniels' top targets, catching 54 passes for 826 yards and seven touchdowns during their time together.

Meanwhile, Daniels threw for 6,725 yards and 57 touchdowns with just seven interceptions across those two seasons. He also rushed for 2,019 yards and 21 touchdowns.

articles.body:
Ever since deciding to not pull the trigger on a trade for a wide receiver, the Steelers' offense has struggled to find success through the air. But even after consecutive losses, Pittsburgh remains in the thick the AFC North hunt.

Adam Schefter Urges the Steelers to Look at Brandon Aiyuk

And since the Steelers still have an opportunity to reach the postseason, ESPN insider Adam Schefter argued they shouldn't give up on acquiring more help at receiver. In fact, Schefter believes Pittsburgh should "check in" on the recently released Brandon Aiyuk.

"How many times have we heard the Pittsburgh Steelers connected to wide receivers the last couple years, including for Brandon Aiyuk?," mentioned Schefter on a recent episode of his podcast. "If the guy that you considered trading for at one point now were a free agent, would it not make sense that the Pittsburgh Steelers would check in?," he added.

Despite his baggage, the former 49ers wide out Aiyuk would be a veteran presence to boost a room that needs reliable production. Aiyuk did surpass 1,000 yards in back-to-back seasons, highlighted by recording 1,342 yards off 75 receptions in 2023. He's caught 294 passes for 4,305 yards throughout his career.

Aiyuk Would Bring Similar Concerns the Steelers Are Already Dealing With

However, the counter is Aiyuk has only played one game since 2024 and he would bring character concerns, something that may enough on its own for the Steelers to turn away, especially while dealing with DK Metcalf's recent antics . Aiyuk had a propensity to post crypto messages on social media in the controversial end of his time in San Francisco.

But with the trade deadline having passed, the Steelers may have no other choice than to bite the bullet and bring in Aiyuk, feeling he's the best of what's available to be signed on the market.

Because quarterback Aaron Rodgers' recent poor play shows he's no longer able to elevate just anyone. Rodgers threw just 143 yards and completed only 51.7% of his throws in Pittsburgh's 38-18 loss to the rival Cincinnati Bengals two weeks ago and then tossed 227, although on 44 pass attempts, falling 19-16 to the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday.

articles.title: YouTube reportedly in negotiations with NFL for 3-game mini-package in 2027
articles.summary: YouTube is reportedly trying to secure a package of NFL games for the 2027 season. According to John Ourand in Puck, YouTube is negotiating for a three-game...
articles.body:
YouTube is reportedly trying to secure a package of NFL games for the 2027 season.

According to John Ourand in Puck , YouTube is negotiating for a three-game mini-package for next season that would include a Christmas Eve game, the extra Saturday Week 17 game that went to NBC this year, and the extra international game that went to Fox in Week 10. Ourand stressed that the talks cannot be characterized as "close," but YouTube is nevertheless kicking the tires on a package after having exited negotiations over the five-game package that ended up going to Netflix this past offseason.

YouTube, of course, has exclusively aired one NFL game in the past: a Week 1 Friday night game from Brazil in 2025 between the Chiefs and Chargers. The global video platform averaged 17.3 million worldwide viewers for that game.

The NFL's talks with YouTube fell through during the offseason after the league attempted to split the five-game package with Netflix. According to reports at the time, YouTube balked at splitting the already limited inventory and decided to walk away. But it appears it's still interested in carving out its own package for next season. YouTube already has exclusive distribution rights for NFL Sunday Ticket, the league's out-of-market package.

Next year, Christmas Day falls on a Saturday, meaning Christmas Eve represents yet another standalone window opportunity for the NFL that Friday night. As Sports Business Journal recently reported, the NFL's Christmas plans for next year are not yet finalized . Netflix is guaranteed at least one game as part of its new media rights deal with the league, and Fox is believed to have a claim on at least one Christmas Day game as well. Like this year, the league could also decide to add a third game on Christmas Day and award it to another broadcaster. Or, it could again offer Netflix a doubleheader on the holiday, which the streamer will do for the third consecutive year next month.

The NFL would like to keep deep-pocketed media companies like YouTube in the fold ahead of what's expected to be a wholesale auction for media rights after the 2029-30 season, when the league can opt out of its current deals with every partner except ESPN, whose exit option kicks in a year later. Selling one-off games keeps the company tethered to the NFL and provides tangible data points to measure engagement as it weighs a bid for a larger package a few years down the line.

To be sure, there is no imminent deal. But the fact that YouTube and the NFL are actively engaged in such talks is noteworthy in it of itself. It shows that YouTube is interested in deepening its relationship with the league, which is good news for the NFL.

articles.title: Bengals CB Facing NFL Punishment for Dirty Hit on Antonio Williams
articles.summary: Bengals CB facing NFL punishment for dirty hit on Commanders WR Antonio Williams. The post Bengals CB Facing NFL Punishment for Dirty Hit on Antonio Williams...
articles.body:
The NFL is in its second season since making the dangerous hip-drop tackle illegal — for some reason, its highly trained officials can't seem to recognize the illegal play in real time.

The latest, most glaring example came in a Week 11 Monday Night Football contest between the Washington Commanders and Cincinnati Bengals, in which Bengals cornerback Dax Hill executed a textbook hip-drop tackle on Commanders rookie wide receiver Antonio Williams … and the officials didn't bat an eye.

The missed call left NFL fans aghast at the inability to regulate a play that has led to some of the NFL's most gruesome injuries.

Williams finished with a career game of 9 receptions for 122 yards, including 2 receptions for 64 yards on the game-winning drive that set up a 26-yard, walk-off field goal by Drew Stevens in a 22-20 Commanders win.

Where Hill's dirty play probably won't be missed? At the offices of the NFL's GameDay Accountability Committee, who hand out fines each week for plays such as this.

NFL Fans React With Disgust at Missed Call

As expected, NFL fans were less than thrilled to see NFL officials miss another hip-drop tackle — especially one that was so obvious.

"Remember when the NFL said they were banning hip-drop tackles?" Barstool Sports wrote on X.

"Considering the NFL made a huge point about calling it, they probably should actually call it," Bad Sports Refs wrote on X .

"Hip-Drop Tackle — EXTREMELY extremely dangerous," NFL writer John Frascella wrote on X . "Wait… … this was NOT called a penalty??? What the (expletive) is going on in this league?"

articles.title: 2027 NFL Mock Draft: Browns land basketball player turned SEC defender
articles.summary: The Browns land one of the biggest risers of the 2027 NFL Draft cycle in a new mock.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns have a good defense. It has helped carry a struggling offense to a 6-4 record and has them on track to make the playoffs. This unit, particularly the back seven, has played at a high level this season.

However, the run defense has been one of the worst in the NFL this year. They are tied for the 5th-worst rushing yards allowed per carry. For a defensive football team, this aspect is definitely a weakness.

I would expect that to be addressed early in the NFL draft this year. People focus on the loss of Myles Garrett and what that means in terms of rushing the passer, but stopping the run and controlling the line of scrimmage is also part of that equation. The Browns are still looking to fill some of that void.

Recently, Justin Melo of Sports Illustrated mocked the Browns a defensive lineman in his latest mock draft. Someone who can get after the passes, but also brings the size that is necessary to anchor against the run. That would be Alabama's Devan Thompkins.

"The Cleveland Browns need to continue investing in defensive lineman, as Myles Garrett obviously hasn't been replaced. Alabama's Devan Thompkins is a very intriguing prospect. Thompkins is big and violent with inside-outside versatility."

At a listed 6 '5 and 300 pounds, Thompkins is very big for a defensive end by today's standards. He can even kick inside and play some defensive tackle. Yet he still has the speed and fluidity to win on the outside as well.

I like the idea of this pick because it solves multiple problems. Getting to opposing quarterbacks will always steal the spotlight, and Thompkins can do that, but being able to shut down the opposing running game is almost as important in today's NFL.

articles.title: AFC North QB stock watch: Jacoby Brissett keeps Ravens in games
articles.summary: The AFC North quarterback market saw some movement in Week 11, with some stocks holding firm and others showing signs of trouble.
articles.body:
The AFC North quarterback picture had a little bit of everything in Week 11. One quarterback continued to make a strong case as the division's best. Another endured a frustrating afternoon against a team that had spent the previous seven weeks searching for a win. Another still delivered a respectable performance that went unrewarded . Some of you may recognize that last guy as the Baltimore Ravens starter, Jacoby Brissett.

Deshaun Watson and company enjoyed a week off. The Cleveland Browns will return to primetime in Week 12, where they'll have another opportunity to make their mark when they return to action.

The AFC North remains a division where quarterback play can swing the conversation quickly, but Week 11 offered another reminder that individual performance and team success don't always travel together. Some stocks are holding steady. Others are showing signs of fatigue, and the difference between a good investment and a costly gamble is becoming clearer as the season progresses.

Sometimes the best move in the market is to sit tight, and that's where Deshaun Watson finds himself after the Browns enjoyed their Week 11 bye. There isn't much to evaluate from an idle week, but Watson and the Browns will return to action with an intriguing primetime matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders.

The break gives Cleveland a chance to regroup before its next assignment. Watson's stock remains on hold until he gets back on the field and provides something new to evaluate.

What looked like a potential value trap on paper after Week 10 has turned into a legitimate value opportunity. Brissett continues to provide the Ravens with solid quarterback play , and his performance against the Carolina Panthers was good enough to keep Baltimore in position to win. Unfortunately, the defense couldn't deliver when the team needed it most.

Brissett completed 24 of 37 passes for 276 yards, one touchdown and one interception. He also added seven rushing yards on two carries while taking two sacks. The interception came on Baltimore's final possession, but it shouldn't overshadow an otherwise productive afternoon from a quarterback who has been asked to keep the offense functioning without Jackson.

The bigger problem is that Baltimore keeps wasting these opportunities. Brissett has shown he can operate the offense and produce enough to win , but the Ravens need considerably more help from their defense. His stock remains on the rise, even if the team's results suggest otherwise.

Week 11 stats: 24-of-37 passing, 276 yards, one touchdown, one interception, two sacks taken, seven rushing yards.

Brissett has thrown for 616 yards in two Baltimore starts, and the Ravens lost those games by a combined five points. He hit Rashod Bateman for a 52-yard touchdown at Carolina, but his last pass came with Baltimore still on its side of midfield and needing a field goal. Linebacker Tyrel Dodson intercepted the throw intended for Bateman, and the Panthers took over with 24 seconds left. Brissett has given the Ravens more production through the air, and that last possession counts in his evaluation, too.

Even a juggernaut can lose a little steam. That's the nature of the NFL: one explosive performance doesn't guarantee the next will be just as impressive. Burrow had a quieter afternoon in Week 11, but there's no reason to start questioning his place atop the AFC North quarterback rankings.

Burrow completed 28 of 40 passes for 300 yards and two touchdowns without throwing an interception. He was sacked three times, but still managed to produce another 300-yard performance while avoiding the costly mistakes that can derail an offense.

His uptrend may have stalled temporarily near resistance, but it hasn't broken down. Burrow remains the division's most accomplished quarterback this season, and one less spectacular outing doesn't change that. The stock is still strong, even if investors might be waiting for the next big jump.

Week 11 stats: 28-of-40 passing, 300 yards, two touchdowns, zero interceptions, three sacks taken.

Burrow helped Cincinnati take a 20-19 lead with 46 seconds left. His 32-yard completion to tight end Mike Gesicki set up Evan McPherson's 56-yard field goal. Washington answered with two completions from Jayden Daniels to Antonio Williams and won on Drew Stevens' 26-yard kick as time expired. Burrow put Cincinnati ahead on its final possession. The Bengals needed one more stop.

Week 11 verdict: Modest Gains With Downside Anxiety

The Pittsburgh Steelers have experienced their share of ups and downs this season, but their Week 11 trip to Philadelphia was particularly disappointing. Facing a Philadelphia Eagles team that had lost seven straight games, Pittsburgh never led and left town with a defeat that raised more questions than it answered.

Rodgers wasn't necessarily the reason the Steelers lost, but he didn't do enough to change the outcome. He completed 30 of 44 passes for 227 yards and one touchdown without an interception. He also took five sacks, although he added 29 rushing yards on five carries.

The veteran avoided turnovers, but the passing production was underwhelming, especially against a defense that had struggled to help Philadelphia win games. Rodgers' stock isn't collapsing, but the latest performance offers little reason for excitement. Pittsburgh needs more from its offense if it expects to remain competitive in the division.

Week 11 stats: 30-of-44 passing, 227 yards, one touchdown, zero interceptions, five sacks taken, 29 rushing yards.

Pittsburgh converted five of 17 third downs against Philadelphia. The Eagles sacked Rodgers five times and held Jaylen Warren to 29 yards rushing. Rodgers kept the Steelers within a field goal, but they spent too much of the afternoon trying to sustain drives without much help from their lead back.

AFC North quarterback stock: Burrow remains the standard

Burrow continues to set the pace in the AFC North, even after a relatively modest outing. Brissett deserves credit for keeping Baltimore's offense competitive under difficult circumstances. The problem for the Ravens is that productive quarterback play hasn't translated into wins. Rodgers and the Steelers have their own concerns after failing to capitalize on an opportunity against Philadelphia.

As mentioned, Watson gets another chance to change the conversation when Cleveland returns from its bye. All eyes will be on that one, as it's a standalone game. With the division's quarterback picture continuing to shift, the next few weeks could reveal plenty about which teams have a reliable foundation under center and which ones are still searching for answers.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers donated $1 million after California’s Camp Fire; how his hometown recovery effort became a bigger mission
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers pledged $1 million on November 21, 2018, to help Butte County in Northern California recover from the Camp Fire.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers pledged $1 million on November 21, 2018, to help Butte County in Northern California recover from the Camp Fire. The fire killed at least 81 people. The Green Bay Packers quarterback grew up in Chico, the city that took in thousands of displaced people after the blaze destroyed Paradise. He sent the money to the North Valley Community Foundation, and State Farm agreed to match it through retweets. Eight years later, the fund he started still pays for school programs, youth sports and housing in a region that is slowly rebuilding.Aaron Rodgers gave $1 million after the Camp Fire hit Chico and ParadiseThe Camp Fire broke out on November 8 and went on to destroy more than 12,600 homes. It became the deadliest wildfire in California history. Paradise, a town of about 30,000, was wiped off the map, and nearby Chico took in tens of thousands of displaced people. Aaron Rodgers' old high school, Pleasant Valley, sat closed for weeks.Thirteen days after the fire started, Rodgers posted a video on Twitter wearing a "Butte Strong" sweatshirt. The message was simple. "Let's help these people begin to heal and rebuild," he said.State Farm, his longtime sponsor, offered $1 for every retweet until November 25, up to $1 million. The Packers added $250,000 to the fund. By Wednesday afternoon the post had passed 30,000 retweets. He routed the money through a local group so decisions on spending stay in Butte County.The tie to Paradise ran deep. Rodgers has said he played football and basketball there as a kid and once lived in Magalia, a smaller town just off it. After Division I schools passed on him, he spent a season at Butte College, which sits near Paradise.How the fund grew into a long-term mission for Butte CountyThe fund was built for more than emergency aid. Its stated focus was kids' programs, youth and high school sports, and housing. Donors piled in, and the total climbed past $3.3 million, according to the San Francisco Chronicle. About $500,000 in grants had gone out by then, mostly to schools, sports programs and housing groups.Aaron Rodgers also donated 375 helmets, enough to outfit the full programs at Chico, Paradise and Pleasant Valley. Paradise coach Rick Prinz said football helped people there feel normal again, something outsiders struggle to grasp.He has kept adding to it. In July 2024, when the Thompson Fire forced 28,000 people out in Butte County, he added $100,000.The grants keep moving. In spring 2026 the program committed $200,000 to 29 north state projects. Soon after, it gave $15,000 to help Paradise High's football team travel to Maui for the Unity Bowl against Lahainaluna, a game between two communities scarred by wildfire. Paradise's goal for the trip was $72,000, so the grant covered about a fifth of it.The money is small next to the loss. More than 12,600 homes burned, and no single fund replaces that. What this one does is cover smaller gaps, like a hotel block for a travelling team or helmets for kids who lost their routine.Aaron Rodgers' fund also sits inside a bigger system. The foundation's wider wildfire fund has put more than $67 million to work for Camp Fire survivors. His fund is a slice, but one with a clear job: kids, sports and housing.None of the later grants match that first $1 million, but together they have kept money moving for years.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders embraced the holiday spirit on Tuesday for some local shoppers.

At Dave's Market in Cleveland, the second-year player bought groceries for several customers at checkout, a video from News 5 Cleveland reporter Camryn Justice showed.

Sanders went around the store and brought more people to the cash registers so he could pay for more people's shopping, including for many who were out to get ready for Thanksgiving.

"I find enjoyment in doing these things and random acts of kindness when people aren't even expecting anything," Sanders said in the news broadcast.

The video shows Sanders going up to customers and pointing to the lines, saying, "I heard they're giving away free groceries up there."

"I think the most important thing is (to) give everybody something to look forward to and have hope," Sanders said. "In all of our lives, everybody's going through the positives, negatives, all different types of things. And sometimes that random act is just what somebody needs."

We wish the entire Ford and Firestone families peace in this time of mourning."

Ford and her husband, William Clay Ford, initially purchased full control of the team in 1963.

Martha eventually assumed sole control of the Lions upon William's death in 2014, as she became increasingly active in the franchise's day-to-day operations. She remained in the role for six years before stepping aside and transitioning to emeritus status while her daughter, Sheila Ford Hamp, took over as principal owner.

The Lions compiled a 45-50-1 record with two playoff appearances during Martha's tenure as primary owner.

In 2017, she made a $100 million investment in renovations for Ford Field.

Two years later, the Lions announced a $600,000 initial financial commitment from Ford, as well as players, for the launch of social justice initiative Detroit Lions Inspire Change. The initiative focuses on scholarship funding, social-educational programs and medical aid/health assistance.

She remained present with the team after her time as principal owner came to an end, as she attended multiple games this season.

Ford is survived by her four children, 14 grandchildren and 17 great-grandchildren.
