articles.title: Aaron Rodgers couldn't play forever, and he might have an unceremonious end at age 42
articles.summary: There were four MVPs, 10 Pro Bowls, a Super Bowl championship, dozens of highlights that defied belief over 22 seasons, and it all seems to end with a quick...
articles.body:
Few players get the John Elway or Peyton Manning sendoff, winning a Super Bowl then announcing their retirement a few weeks or months later.

Still, it seemed like Aaron Rodgers would have a gentler ending to his great career than a short statement at 11:10 p.m. on a Tuesday.

There were four MVPs, 10 Pro Bowls, a Super Bowl championship, dozens of highlights that defied belief over 22 seasons, and it all seems to end with a quick statement from the team after most of Pittsburgh had already gone to sleep.

It's not like Rodgers has played great this season, which he said will be his last in the NFL. Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy was asked this week if Rodgers was still the team's starter, so it wasn't completely out of the blue that he got benched.

It was abrupt, and with some unusual timing. There was no time to celebrate the end of a legendary career or even realize that the snaps he took Sunday might be his last.

It's just done, barring some other turn of events over the final few weeks of the season.

Rodgers played OK this year. The Steelers couldn't have expected much more from a quarterback who will turn 43 on Dec. 2. No other quarterback, other than Tom Brady, had any reasonable level of success at Rodgers' age.

Rodgers threw for 2,241 yards and 16 touchdowns with six interceptions in 10 games. The Steelers won six of those games and if the season ended now, they'd be in the playoffs. Rodgers wasn't great, often throwing short as he did last season, which was reflected in him having the fourth-worst EPA ( expected points added ) among all qualified quarterbacks. It still didn't seem like he'd be benched.

It wasn't like the Steelers were giving the job to a hotshot rookie who will excite the fan base. Rudolph has been decent as a backup throughout his career, and he had a stretch in 2023 when the Steelers won all three of his starts that helped them to the playoffs. But the Steelers didn't feel any urgency to see what Rudolph can do. They just apparently felt Rodgers had already hit the age cliff and they saw it over the last two games.

After a solid start to the season there were two miserable performances from Rodgers and the team. He threw incomplete on his first seven passes in a blowout loss to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 10. That was the first time in his career he had started 0-for-7. Pittsburgh's loss on Sunday in Philadelphia was ugly, with the Steelers not scoring a touchdown until the final two minutes. Undrafted rookie Max Hurleman, making his NFL debut, might have become a trivia answer: He caught the Steelers' only touchdown against the Eagles, and it might end up being the final touchdown pass of Rodgers' career. As it stands, that could be the final play of Rodgers' career. Pittsburgh never got the ball back after that.

The Steelers were slumping. But the way the week unfolded makes the benching quite odd.

The strange circumstances with Rodgers' benching

The Steelers have a short week. When asked Monday about Rodgers and possibly benching him, McCarthy gave a terse answer: "Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback." Then less than 48 hours later, with a game less than three days away, the Steelers made a change at quarterback.

The benching likely happened before 11 p.m. on a Tuesday but that's when the NFL world found out, making it one of the odder quarterback announcements in recent memory. And the decision to demote Rodgers all the way to at least No. 3 on the depth chart (the Steelers are the rare team that carries four quarterbacks) was made by a coach with whom Rodgers won a Super Bowl with at the end of the 2010 season. There wasn't anything pleasant about the move or how it was handled, and an NFL legend like Rodgers probably deserved better. But the league isn't much on sentiment, especially for teams on two-game losing streaks in a playoff race.

Maybe there will be more details to the benching, other than a coach who definitively said Monday that Rodgers was his quarterback completely changing his mind on a Tuesday (a day when the Steelers had a walkthrough practice), three days before his team plays the 8-2 Broncos.

Rodgers has spent most of his career, particularly the final few years of it, living in defiance. His confidence never wavered, whether talking about politics, criticizing the media or showing up teammates and even his coach on the field when he felt he wasn't at fault for a bad play. It never seemed he'd leave the game unless it was on his terms. Perhaps he gets a start later in the season if Rudolph doesn't play well or there are injuries or simply to give an all-time great a better sendoff than a social media blast late in the evening.

But there's a good chance we've suddenly seen the last of Rodgers on a football field, especially with the team making sure the world knew he wouldn't even be active Friday. The NFL can be a cold business, even for someone who was one of the faces of the league for a couple decades.

articles.title: In shocking move, Steelers bench Aaron Rodgers and will start Mason Rudolph vs. Broncos
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers’ long, accomplished career took a stunning twist in his final season.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers’ long, accomplished career took a stunning twist in his final season. The four-time NFL MVP has been benched by the Pittsburgh Steelers, and Mason Rudolph will start against the Denver Broncos on Friday. Rodgers will be inactive for the game, the team said in a statement late Tuesday night. Rodgers, who turns 43 next week, has completed 60.9% of his passes for 2,241 yards with 16 touchdown passes and six interceptions. The Steelers (6-4) have lost two in a row, and Rodgers struggled in both games, though the receiving corps has been depleted. Rudolph has started just 19 games in seven seasons with the Steelers and Tennessee Titans, going 9-9-1. He went 3-0 down the stretch in 2023 while filling in for Kenny Pickett and led Pittsburgh to the playoffs. The Steelers lost a wild-card playoff game to Buffalo that season. Rodgers returned for his 22nd season in the NFL to reunite with coach Mike McCarthy, who replaced Mike Tomlin. Rodgers and McCarthy won a Super Bowl together in Green Bay following the 2010 season. On Monday, McCarthy said Rodgers is the starter. That changed a day later. Rodgers wasn’t listed on the team’s injury report and spoke to reporters after practice. It’s a shocking move by the Steelers, considering Rodgers’ relationship with McCarthy — he played a role in his hiring — and the alternative. Rodgers has an 86.6 passer rating, which is the lowest in his career. Rudolph is a career backup with a passer rating of 84.3. But the Steelers are looking for someone to spark an offense that’s 23rd in total yards (310.4 per game), 22nd in passing (198.6) and is averaging 21.4 points. Pittsburgh is tied with Cleveland and currently holds a wild-card spot in the AFC with a one-game lead over New England (5-5). Rodgers has been sacked 31 times this season, including five times in a 19-16 loss at Philadelphia on Sunday. He completed 30 of 44 passes for 227 yards and one TD with no picks. Rodgers actually led the team in rushing with 29 yards, including a 12-yard scamper. Wide receiver DK Metcalf had just one catch on four targets before he was ejected from the game. Veteran wideout Michael Pittman Jr. didn’t play. Pittsburgh’s leading receiver against the Eagles was Max Hurleman, a guy making his NFL debut. It’s uncertain whether Rodgers will ask for his release so he can have an opportunity to join another team to close out his career. Daniel Jones also is a free agent after he was released last week by the Indianapolis Colts. Rodgers led the Steelers to a 10-6 record last season in his first year with the team. They lost 30-6 to Houston in a wild-card game. Rodgers ranks third on the NFL’s all-time list with 543 touchdown passes, fifth in passing yards at 68,515 and fifth with 5,916 complete passes. His 101.6 passer rating is fourth-best.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers benched by Pittsburgh Steelers for game with Denver Broncos as Mason Rudolph starts at quarterback
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers has struggled in the Pittsburgh Steelers' back-to-back defeats to the Cincinnati Bengals and the Philadelphia Eagles; quarterback, who turns 43 next week, has been sacked 31 times this season; Mason Rudolph has started only 19 games in seven seasons
articles.body:
Rodgers, who turns 43 next week, has struggled during the Steelers' back-to-back defeats to the Cincinnati Bengals and the Philadelphia Eagles.

Pittsburgh confirmed in a statement that the veteran quarterback will be "inactive", despite head coach Mike McCarthy saying on Monday that he remained the starter.

Rodgers is amid his 22nd and final NFL season, having reunited with McCarthy after the two previously won the Super Bowl together at the Green Bay Packers in 2010.

He was key in McCarthy being hired to take over from Mike Tomlin.

Rudolph has started only 19 games in seven seasons with the Steelers and the Tennessee Titans, so this is a big call from Pittsburgh, even considering Rodger's flagging numbers.

Rodgers has completed under 61 per cent of pass attempts this season, marking one of his worst campaigns since he became a full-time starter with Green Bay in 2008.

The quarterback has been sacked 31 times, surpassing last year's total of 21 already, and leads the league with 257 yards lost in those sacks.

Earlier this week, McCarthy said of Rodgers when discussing Pittsburgh's successive defeats: "When you talk about the quarterback position, I think there's things offensively we need to do better and that always benefits and leads into quarterback play.

"I just need him to just keep ploughing away. We got a lot of work to do."

articles.title: Mike McCarthy’s Aaron Rodgers comments preceded Mason Rudolph’s unexpected Pittsburgh Steelers starting opportunity
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers have finally granted some fans’ wishes by benching Aaron Rodgers.
articles.body: The Pittsburgh Steelers have finally granted some fans’ wishes by benching Aaron Rodgers. After losing two games in a row, the team didn’t want a third loss to further jeopardize their fading playoff hopes.Since returning from their bye week - which may have been an ayahuasca retreat for Rodgers [though, he probably doesn’t do those during the season] -the Steelers have suffered back-to-back defeats: one to a Super Bowl contender, the Cincinnati Bengals, and another to the Philadelphia Eagles, who were playing without their franchise quarterback, Jalen Hurts. Instead, Joe Milton III started for Philadelphia in Week 11 against Pittsburgh.This loss likely left Rodgers, the coaches, and the front office questioning whether their 42-year-old starter can still perform on the gridiron.As a result, according to NFL insider Tom Pelissero, Pittsburgh head coach Mike McCarthy decided to rest the veteran QB and give Mason Rudolph - their 2018 third-round pick - a chance to prove himself.Mason Rudolph gets Steelers starting nod just a day after Mike McCarthy backed Aaron RodgersHead coach Mike McCarthy believed in Aaron Rodgers until Monday. When asked about making a QB change that day, McCarthy sounded confused that the question was even raised.A reporter asked if the team was considering a change at quarterback because the offense was struggling, and McCarthy adamantly stated that Rodgers was their guy. Yet by Tuesday night, they had benched Rodgers and named Mason Rudolph the starter.The reporter had asked, “You have four quarterbacks on the active roster, and with the offense struggling the way it has, do you consider using any of the others or mixing things up to give the offense a different look?”To which, the coach replied, “Like a quarterback halfback pass or something? Are you talking about trick plays, or…?”“Or putting Mason in when—” the reporter began, before being interrupted by McCarthy: “No, Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback.”Rudolph is a 31-year-old NFL quarterback who played college football for Oklahoma State before spending seven seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers and one with the Tennessee Titans.The 6-foot-5, 235-pounder has accumulated modest stats over the past nine years: 476 completions on 742 attempts for 4,927 passing yards, 30 touchdowns, and 22 interceptions.The Northwestern alum’s career passer rating is 84.3, with a 64.2% completion rate. He holds a 9–9–1 record in the regular season and is 0–1 in the playoffs. During his lone season with the Titans in 2024, he struggled to find success, going just 1–4 as a starter.It wouldn’t be surprising if the Steelers lose their upcoming Week 12 matchup against the Denver Broncos, given Rudolph’s past starting record. Still, we never know - this is a midseason opportunity, and he will likely be eager to turn his NFL career around.This move could also mean Pittsburgh is resting the retirement-prone Rodgers or saving him for bigger games - assuming they make it that far. Ultimately, the QB switch raises serious questions about their chances of reaching the 2026 playoffs.Pittsburgh Steelers’ 2026 NFL playoff chancesThe AFC playoff picture entering Week 12 puts the Pittsburgh Steelers in seventh place, behind the Buffalo Bills, Denver Broncos, Jacksonville Jaguars, Cincinnati Bengals, Kansas City Chiefs, and Cleveland Browns.The Steelers have a 62% chance of making the 2026 NFL playoffs. If they win Week 12 vs. the Denver Broncos, their chances soar to 77%. If they lose, their chances drop to 54%.They have a less than 1% chance of claiming the No. 1 seed and a 9% chance of winning the AFC North - something the Aaron Rodgers-led Steelers did last season, finishing first with a 10–7 regular-season record.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: The Eagles visit the Cowboys in the middle game of the NFL’s Thanksgiving tripleheader. Get kickoff times, TV channels and crews for all three
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys have the middle game of the NFL's Thanksgiving tripleheader Thursday, Nov. 26. The NFC East rivals kick off at 4:30 p.m. ET on Fox, with a free live stream on Tubi. The Chicago Bears and Detroit Lions open the day on CBS, and the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills close it on NBC.

Kevin Burkhardt, Tom Brady, Erin Andrews and Tom Rinaldi

Mike Tirico, Cris Collinsworth and Melissa Stark

The Bears and CBS confirmed the early broadcast; Fox will carry the afternoon game, and NBC will air the nightcap, with Spanish-language coverage on Telemundo.

Chicago and Detroit enter the opener at 8-2, giving the winner a one-game edge over the other in the NFC North. Jim Nantz will call the game for CBS, with J.J. Watt providing analysis and Tracy Wolfson reporting from the sideline. The broadcast also streams on Paramount+.

Philadelphia (3-7) ended a seven-game losing streak with a 19-16 win over Pittsburgh on Sunday. Dallas (5-6) won the first meeting 38-21 in Week 7 and enters the rematch after scoring 51 points against Tennessee. Dak Prescott threw four touchdown passes and ran for another in that win.

Kevin Burkhardt will handle play-by-play from AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, with Tom Brady on analysis and Erin Andrews and Tom Rinaldi on the sidelines. Tubi's pregame coverage begins at 4 p.m. ET. Viewers can watch free by signing in or creating a free account. Fox Deportes will carry the game in Spanish.

Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs (8-2) visit Josh Allen and the Bills (9-1) in the nightcap at Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park, N.Y. NBC's coverage begins at 8 p.m. ET, 20 minutes before kickoff. Mike Tirico will call the game alongside Cris Collinsworth, with Melissa Stark reporting from the sideline and Terry McAulay serving as rules analyst. The game will also stream on Peacock.
